body:
## Problem Statement

Java teams that depend on the iText 7.2.6-era product suite need a migration path that keeps Java 8 support and avoids AGPL or proprietary runtime dependencies. PDFBox provides a suitable permissively licensed low-level engine, but it does not provide the high-level layout, typography, conversion, sanitization, conformance, Office, OCR, or migration surface required to replace the complete suite.

Users need a deliberately independent implementation that reduces migration cost without making false promises about unchanged imports, binary linkage, byte-identical files, or unsupported capabilities. They also need objective evidence for compatibility, safe processing of hostile PDFs, stable lifecycle and failure behavior, and a reproducible Maven Central release process.

## Solution

Build Folio PDF by ZeroCloud as an Apache-2.0, clean-room Java component suite under net.zerocloud. Fix the comparison target to the Reference Suite: iText Core 7.2.6 plus the matching pdfSweep, pdfCalligraph, pdfXFA, pdfHTML, pdfOCR, pdfOptimizer, pdfRender, and pdfOffice versions.

Expose a coherent Native Interface centered on a transactional Document Workflow, and provide a separate Migration Facade that maps familiar iText 7-era concepts into that interface under a project-owned namespace. Deliver Capability Parity incrementally. Foundation Release 0.1.0 establishes the Document Engine, full Foundation Composition Profile, rendering, password encryption, existing-signature protection, stable migration coverage, hostile-input handling, and acceptance infrastructure. Later dependency-gated releases complete the remaining Core and add-on capabilities.

Treat the Capability Matrix and Facade Surface Manifest as machine-readable authorities. A capability may be described as compatible only after its capability-specific Acceptance Profile has complete independent evidence.

## User Stories

1. As a Java 8 application developer, I want artifacts that genuinely run on Java 8, so that I can migrate without upgrading my production JVM.
2. As a developer on a later JDK, I want the same artifacts tested on JDK 11, 17, and 21, so that runtime upgrades do not require a different library line.
3. As a Maven user, I want all first-party modules available under net.zerocloud and selectable through a BOM, so that dependency management is predictable.
4. As a PDF author, I want to create documents with explicit page sizes, margins, and area breaks, so that I can control document structure.
5. As a PDF author, I want mixed-content paragraphs with leading, alignment, indents, tabs, keep behavior, and widow/orphan behavior, so that business documents paginate correctly.
6. As a PDF author, I want fixed and automatic tables with row and column spans, so that complex tabular documents can be represented.
7. As a PDF author, I want repeated table headers and footers, overflow handling, page splitting, relayout, and incremental large-table flushing, so that long reports remain usable.
8. As a multilingual author, I want Latin, Greek, Cyrillic, CJK, Arabic, Hebrew, Devanagari, and Thai shaping and layout, so that text is logically and visually correct.
9. As a document generator, I want every barcode generation mode in the iText 7.2.6 Core barcodes module, so that existing labels and forms can migrate.
10. As a PDF consumer, I want to open files from paths, streams, channels, and bounded byte sources, so that the library fits different application architectures.
11. As a PDF editor, I want to add, remove, move, and copy pages, so that I can modify existing documents.
12. As a batch processor, I want to merge and split PDFs, so that I can assemble and distribute document sets.
13. As an extraction user, I want text, image, page, metadata, and structural extraction, so that downstream systems can inspect documents.
14. As an advanced PDF developer, I want backend-neutral low-level PDF Values and Object References, so that I can perform advanced edits without depending on PDFBox classes.
15. As an advanced PDF developer, I want validated Document Patches, so that low-level changes cannot bypass lifecycle and preservation rules.
16. As an editor, I want unknown objects and resources preserved when safe, so that unrelated content is not silently lost.
17. As an editor, I want an operation rejected when unknown content cannot be preserved safely, so that the library never pretends a destructive edit is safe.
18. As a caller, I want to choose REWRITE or INCREMENTAL explicitly, so that publication semantics are not inferred unpredictably.
19. As a signature-sensitive user, I want signed documents read-only by default, so that edits cannot silently invalidate signatures.
20. As a signature-sensitive user, I want permitted incremental changes only when signature and DocMDP rules allow them, so that earlier revisions remain intact.
21. As a renderer user, I want pages rendered to bounded images with explicit scale, DPI, crop, color, and alpha options, so that rendering is deterministic.
22. As a security-conscious author, I want PDF 1.7 with AES-256 as the default output policy, so that obsolete algorithms are not selected accidentally.
23. As a migration user, I want to read supported legacy encryption and explicitly opt into Legacy Security Mode for legacy output, so that compatibility does not weaken defaults.
24. As a PDF 2.0 user, I want explicit PDF 2.0 output and PDF 1.0 through 2.0 input support, so that version selection is controlled.
25. As a forms developer, I want AcroForm creation, filling, appearance handling, flattening, and XFDF support, so that interactive workflows can migrate.
26. As an XFA user, I want XFA processing behind the Forms context, so that dynamic form workflows can be supported in a later dependency-gated phase.
27. As a Trust user, I want public-key encryption, signing, verification, external signing, HSM, TSA, OCSP, CRL, DSS, LTV, and PAdES capabilities, so that document authenticity workflows can migrate.
28. As an archival specialist, I want PDF/A-1, PDF/A-2, and PDF/A-3 creation checks and independently validated outputs, so that archival documents meet the fixed baseline.
29. As an accessibility specialist, I want tagged and metadata-assisted PDF/UA-1 creation, so that accessible output can be produced within the fixed Reference Conformance Set.
30. As an accessibility reviewer, I want machine and human accessibility evidence kept separate, so that automation is not misrepresented as complete accessibility proof.
31. As an HTML conversion user, I want HTML and CSS transformed through layout, Forms, SVG, and styled XML capabilities, so that web content can become PDF.
32. As an SVG user, I want SVG converted into reusable PDF graphics, so that vector assets remain sharp.
33. As an OCR user, I want PDF pages rendered, recognized by a selected provider, and rebuilt with a searchable text layer, so that scanned PDFs become searchable.
34. As an Office conversion user, I want Word, Excel, and PowerPoint documents converted through a replaceable provider, so that the initial LibreOffice implementation can later be replaced without API changes.
35. As a sanitization user, I want true removal of sensitive content rather than black rectangles or annotations, so that redaction is irreversible.
36. As an optimization user, I want images, fonts, streams, color spaces, and structures optimized, so that file size can be reduced without invalid claims.
37. As an offline operator, I want the default distribution to work without a remote service, so that document content remains local.
38. As an integrator, I want OCR, rendering, Office, native shaping, commercial, and remote engines represented as Capability Providers, so that deployment and licensing choices are explicit.
39. As a privacy-sensitive operator, I want explicit authorization before content is sent to a remote provider, so that document disclosure is never implicit.
40. As a server operator, I want explicit limits for bytes, pages, objects, nesting, decompression, pixels, memory, temporary storage, time, and concurrency, so that hostile documents cannot consume unbounded resources.
41. As a multi-tenant operator, I want hostile input processed in a Hardened Worker Profile, so that a parser failure is isolated from the application process.
42. As a desktop user, I want the same Document Workflow available in-process, so that trusted workloads do not pay IPC complexity.
43. As an API user, I want Commands to preserve order and Queries to observe all preceding changes, so that workflow behavior is understandable.
44. As an IPC user, I want mutation batching and query barriers, so that the Worker does not require one round trip per operation.
45. As an operator, I want uncertain commits resolved through transaction status rather than blind retry, so that output is not duplicated.
46. As an API user, I want stable checked Document Failure codes with safe diagnostics, so that applications can handle operational failures without depending on backend exceptions.
47. As a caller, I want resources opened by the library closed by the library and caller-supplied streams left open, so that ownership is predictable.
48. As a publisher, I want path outputs staged and atomically moved where supported, so that failed workflows do not replace good files.
49. As a multi-output user, I want a Publication Receipt for every target, so that committed, failed, and unattempted destinations are explicit.
50. As a concurrent application, I want a reusable thread-safe Document Workflow and thread-confined Sessions, so that separate documents can run in parallel safely.
51. As an iText migration engineer, I want familiar type and method shapes under net.zerocloud.pdf.itext7, so that import prefixes and call sites can be migrated mechanically where coverage exists.
52. As an iText migration engineer, I want stable and preview Facades to be mutually exclusive, so that experimental mappings cannot be selected accidentally.
53. As an iText migration engineer, I want compile-time surface coverage linked to behavioral evidence, so that a compiling method does not imply unsupported behavior.
54. As a migration planner, I want a generated Capability Matrix, so that I can see supported, limited, experimental, and planned capabilities.
55. As a migration planner, I want a generated Facade Surface Manifest, so that I can measure source migration effort independently of behavioral coverage.
56. As a user, I want capability-specific tolerances rather than one global pixel threshold, so that compatibility criteria fit the behavior being tested.
57. As a user, I want syntax, standards, semantic, visual, and required human evidence kept as separate chains, so that one tool cannot certify the whole product.
58. As a typography maintainer, I want hash-pinned reference fonts and versioned HarfBuzz profiles on four platforms, so that shaping evidence is reproducible.
59. As a contributor, I want clear clean-room and provenance rules, so that my work can be accepted without contaminating the Apache-2.0 project.
60. As an implementer, I want closed-product comparisons isolated behind a Compatibility Curator, so that I do not receive proprietary implementation details.
61. As a maintainer, I want dependency gates recorded in the Capability Matrix, so that downstream work cannot claim compatibility before prerequisites.
62. As a maintainer, I want one Release Train during 0.x, so that module versions remain coherent.
63. As a user of 0.x, I want source-breaking changes documented with migration notes, so that early API evolution remains manageable.
64. As a user of 1.0 and later, I want semantic versioning enforced, so that public compatibility is predictable.
65. As a Maven Central consumer, I want binaries, sources, Javadocs, signatures, and checksums, so that artifacts are inspectable and verifiable.
66. As a supply-chain reviewer, I want a CycloneDX SBOM, license report, vulnerability report, and reproducible-build evidence, so that releases can be audited.
67. As a security reporter, I want a private vulnerability channel, so that parser and cryptographic defects can be disclosed safely.
68. As a release engineer, I want Central credentials and signing material available only after protected-environment approval, so that ordinary CI cannot access publishing secrets.
69. As a release engineer, I want the complete GPG fingerprint pinned, so that the wrong local key cannot sign a release.
70. As a release engineer, I want upload and Central validation separated from irreversible publication, so that the first 0.x releases receive a final human review.
71. As a user, I want authoritative English specifications and a Chinese usage guide, so that contracts remain consistent while Chinese-speaking users have practical documentation.
72. As a project maintainer, I want public non-affiliation notices, so that Folio PDF by ZeroCloud is not confused with LibrePDF OpenPDF or Apryse iText.
73. As a server operator, I want acceptance at approximately 5,000 pages and 1 GiB with controlled spill, so that large bounded workloads are supported without promising unlimited streaming.
74. As a privacy reviewer, I want logs to omit filenames, content, metadata, credentials, private keys, and raw backend exceptions, so that operational visibility does not leak sensitive data.
75. As a community member, I want contributors to retain copyright under DCO and Apache-2.0 inbound terms, so that participation does not require copyright assignment.

## Implementation Decisions

- The fixed Reference Suite is iText Core 7.2.6, pdfSweep 3.0.2, pdfCalligraph 3.0.2, pdfXFA 3.0.4, pdfHTML 4.0.5, pdfOCR 2.0.2, pdfOptimizer 2.0.2, pdfRender 2.0.4, and pdfOffice 2.0.5.
- Capability Parity means supported counterparts for the fixed suite. It excludes unchanged imports, binary linkage, byte-identical output, identical backend exceptions, and an automatically moving target.
- Implementation is clean-room and Apache-2.0. iText source and resources may not be copied or adapted, and closed add-ons may not be reverse-engineered.
- Public standards, public API documentation, project-owned fixtures, and legally approved black-box evidence are allowed. Standards remain the correctness authority.
- The public identity is Folio PDF by ZeroCloud. Java packages use net.zerocloud.pdf and artifacts use net.zerocloud:pdf-*.
- The canonical public repository and issue tracker are zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf. GitHub Issues use the default needs-triage, needs-info, ready-for-agent, ready-for-human, and wontfix vocabulary.
- Java 8 is a runtime contract. Maven builds use a Java-8-compatible Maven 3.9 release and compile with release 8; tests run on JDK 8, 11, 17, and 21.
- All first-party 0.x artifacts share one Release Train managed by pdf-bom. Unimplemented placeholder artifacts are not published.
- Deep modules are organized around Document Engine, Composition, Forms, Trust, Conformance, Conversion, Sanitization, and Migration rather than copying Reference Suite packaging.
- The first-party artifact families are pdf-bom, pdf-document, pdf-composition, pdf-forms, pdf-trust, pdf-conformance, pdf-conversion, pdf-sanitization, pdf-migration-itext7, pdf-provider-*, pdf-acceptance, and pdf-testkit.
- Capability dependency cycles are forbidden. Acceptance and test artifacts never enter production runtime.
- The Native Interface is centered on DocumentWorkflow.execute with a caller-side Document Work callback and a thread-confined Document Session.
- A Workflow Request contains named sources, a primary source, named publication targets, Save Mode, execution policy, resource limits, credentials, and provider preferences.
- A Workflow Outcome contains the caller result, capability and execution information, safe diagnostics, and per-target Publication Receipts.
- The callback always runs in the caller process, including under the Hardened Worker Profile. Workers never receive lambdas or user bytecode.
- Document Commands are project-defined, versioned, ordered, batchable mutation values. Document Queries are project-defined ordering barriers that observe all prior Commands.
- Arbitrary user implementations, Java Serialization, reflection class names, scripts, arbitrary URIs, and backend objects are rejected at the execution boundary.
- The core API is synchronous. Deadlines, cancellation tokens, and sanitized progress events are explicit; callers may use their own Executor for asynchronous composition.
- The Workflow Environment is immutable and thread-safe and owns provider registrations, command/query codecs, reference fonts, temporary storage, worker launch, Clock, Locale, time zone, SecureRandom, and default policy.
- There are no implicit system fonts, default Locale, default time zone, or network calls in compatibility evidence.
- The Document Engine owns a backend-neutral PDF Value model covering null, boolean, number, string, name, array, dictionary, stream, and indirect reference.
- Small values may be immutable and detached. Large streams and traversals are bounded lazy Session views addressed by Object References and invalid after Session close.
- Low-level changes use validated Document Patches. PDFBox COS and PD types are never public contracts.
- REWRITE and INCREMENTAL are explicit Save Modes. Unsigned ordinary edits default to REWRITE.
- Signed files are read-only by default. Only proven permitted changes may use explicit incremental publication.
- Unknown content and resources are preserved when safe; the operation fails when safe preservation cannot be guaranteed.
- Path inputs opened by the module are closed by the module. Caller-provided streams and channels remain caller-owned. Byte and Worker inputs are copied or staged under limits.
- All products are staged and validated before publication. Path targets use atomic replacement where supported. Stream failures report possible partial output. There is no global transaction across multiple targets.
- Document Failure is a checked operational contract with stable codes, capability identifiers, and safe diagnostics. Programming errors remain unchecked, while caller runtime exceptions abort and propagate unchanged.
- The same Native Interface supports In-Process and Hardened Worker execution. Hostile multi-tenant input requires the Worker.
- The first Worker is a local-only child process with a versioned, authenticated, length-bounded protocol, transaction IDs, deadlines, checksums, bounded chunking or staging, and crash recovery.
- Each Worker transaction uses a private restricted temporary root. Worker networking is disabled; remote providers are brokered by the parent and require explicit disclosure consent.
- The default Foundation backend is PDFBox 3.0.8, hidden inside pdf-document. No public backend SPI or API/implementation artifact split is introduced until a second real backend exists.
- ICU4J 77.1 handles Unicode segmentation, bidi, script and line-break behavior; it is not treated as a shaping engine.
- OkapiBarcode 0.5.6 is the default encoder, with project-owned PDF vector rendering for all Reference Suite barcode modes.
- TwelveMonkeys is optional and used only where additional image decoding is required after license review.
- High-level layout, pagination, tables, font fallback, shaping orchestration, hyphenation, resource reuse, image policy, and color policy are owned by Folio PDF.
- Complex shaping uses a project-owned HarfBuzz native adapter. HarfBuzz is not bundled and is certified on Linux x86-64, Windows x86-64, macOS x86-64, and macOS arm64.
- Typography evidence uses hash-pinned static Noto Sans, CJK SC/TC/JP/KR, Arabic, Hebrew, Devanagari, and Thai fonts with OFL notices. System and online fonts are not evidence inputs.
- Foundation reads PDF 1.0 through 2.0 and supported legacy password encryption, writes PDF 1.7 with AES-256 by default, and supports explicit PDF 2.0 output.
- Obsolete output algorithms require Legacy Security Mode.
- Foundation recognizes and protects existing signatures but does not create or validate them.
- Public-key encryption, signatures, certificate chains, external signing, HSM, TSA, OCSP, CRL, DSS, LTV, and PAdES belong to the later Trust module.
- Foundation makes no FIPS claim. A future FIPS Distribution must pin a certified provider, JVM, platform, startup mode, and evidence, with no normal-provider coexistence or fallback.
- The Reference Conformance Set is PDF/A-1A/1B, PDF/A-2A/2B/2U, PDF/A-3A/3B/3U, and tagged plus metadata-assisted PDF/UA-1 creation.
- Creation Checks and Independent Validation are separate concepts. PDF/A-4, PDF/UA-2, and a public PDF/UA validator are not part of the fixed baseline.
- Conversion uses replaceable Capability Providers with project-owned requests and results. Providers declare execution mode, engine version, license and distribution facts, availability, and limits.
- The initial OCR provider is Tesseract CLI. Core rendering and searchable text-layer construction remain owned by Folio PDF.
- The default runtime renderer is PDFBox Renderer. Independent PDFium rendering is used for visual acceptance.
- The initial Office provider is a user-installed LibreOffice headless CLI. LibreOffice is not bundled, and fidelity is judged through pinned acceptance corpora.
- Sanitization must remove underlying content; overlays and annotations do not count as secure redaction.
- The Migration Facade keeps reference package suffixes beneath net.zerocloud.pdf.itext7 and lowers migration cost without preserving imports or linkage.
- pdf-migration-itext7 contains only compatible mappings. pdf-migration-itext7-preview is a mutually exclusive superset containing compatible and experimental mappings.
- The project does not publish a complete surface made of unsupported runtime-throwing stubs.
- capability-matrix.yaml is the behavioral authority. facade-surface.yaml is the source-surface authority. Generated documentation links them in both directions.
- Capability states are planned, experimental, compatible, and limited. Compatible requires complete Acceptance Evidence.
- During 0.x, public source-breaking changes require migration notes. From 1.0, semantic versioning governs public compatibility.
- Foundation Release 0.1.0 includes Document Engine, the complete Foundation Composition Profile, page rendering, password encryption, existing-signature protection, matching Stable Migration Facade coverage, hostile-input handling, and acceptance infrastructure.
- Remaining Core work opens Forms, Trust, Conformance, SVG, and styled XML after verified prerequisites.
- Sanitization, optimization, OCR, and XFA may proceed in parallel after their own Dependency Gates.
- HTML conversion requires compatible Forms, Layout, SVG, and styled XML; advanced scripts additionally require shaping.
- Office conversion is last in the current advisory order because it benefits from mature layout, typography, image, and rendering evidence.
- The project uses Apache-2.0, DCO, contributor provenance, no copyright assignment, and the notice identity Folio PDF by ZeroCloud contributors.
- The Lead Maintainer is initially the project founder under ZeroCloud SDK. The temporary public and security contact is mabaiqiu@gmail.com.
- A Compatibility Curator separate from implementers is required for counsel-approved closed-product black-box evidence. The role is currently vacant, so dependent closed-product evidence remains planned.
- Formal artifacts publish to Maven Central with required POM metadata, sources, Javadocs, signatures, checksums, SBOM, license report, vulnerability report, and reproducibility evidence.
- The Central Publisher plugin uses server id central, does not auto-publish during 0.x, and waits for successful validation before a human performs the immutable publication step.
- Maven GPG signing pins primary fingerprint C5149FD6B5EF7C2126F1FD0FCC1A12E348E171D8 and enforces Maven GPG best practices.
- Local Central and GPG material remains outside the repository with owner-only directory and file permissions. The private key is imported without generating a replacement and verified through a detached-signature round trip.
- Current GPG inspection proves the key material is parseable and the system entropy pool is initialized; no entropy daemon or kernel random configuration change is planned.
- GitHub Actions stores Central username, Central password, armored private key, and GPG passphrase as protected Environment Secrets. Ordinary CI never receives them.
- Release actions are pinned to immutable commit SHAs, use minimum permissions and a single release concurrency group, and require protected-environment approval.
- English README, Javadoc, ADRs, Capability specifications, and API contracts are authoritative. A Chinese usage guide is maintained for users.
- Public documentation prominently disclaims affiliation with LibrePDF OpenPDF and Apryse iText.

## Testing Decisions

- The highest and primary test seam is observable behavior through DocumentWorkflow.execute. Tests supply public requests, Commands and Queries and assert outcomes, Publication Receipts, files, stable failures, resource ownership, and lifecycle behavior.
- In-Process and Hardened Worker adapters run the same Document Workflow contract suite. Worker tests add batching, query barriers, protocol compatibility, timeouts, cancellation, crash recovery, uncertain commit lookup, malformed messages, and resource-limit enforcement.
- The Migration Facade is tested at its public surface by invoking mapped behavior and asserting the same Native Interface outcomes. Tests do not assert internal delegation classes.
- Provider-specific contract tests exist only at real external Capability Provider seams. PDFBox, ICU4J, OkapiBarcode, and ordinary internal helpers do not receive artificial public seams solely for mocking.
- Good tests assert semantic structure, page order, extracted values, layout breaks, geometry, rendered appearance, conformance findings, publication state, or stable errors. They do not assert PDFBox object identity, private method calls, internal batching details, temporary filenames, or byte ordering.
- Syntax evidence uses an external qpdf process and cannot alone prove standards compliance.
- PDF/A and machine-testable PDF/UA evidence uses an independently versioned veraPDF process with explicit flavour and recorded rule or clause findings.
- Project-owned semantic and structural assertions verify the PDF object graph, page sequence, streams, text order, resource behavior, accessibility structure, barcode payloads, and feature-specific semantics.
- Visual evidence renders with a pinned independent PDFium tool, then compares fixed-size images with a pinned ImageMagick configuration and capability-specific thresholds.
- PDFBox Renderer may provide secondary evidence but cannot be the sole visual oracle for a PDFBox-backed implementation.
- PDF/UA Acceptance Profiles combine machine findings with the applicable Matterhorn human checklist. Missing required human review yields INDETERMINATE.
- Acceptance Profiles pin corpus commits, external tool versions or image digests, fonts, hashes, DPI, page boxes, color settings, expected rule IDs, thresholds, and human evidence.
- A PASS requires all mandatory evidence chains. Missing tools, renderer conflicts, absent platform evidence, or incomplete human review yield INDETERMINATE rather than PASS.
- iText output is never the correctness golden. Counsel-approved black-box evidence may discover migration gaps but only the Compatibility Curator may produce it.
- Foundation typography tests compare glyph IDs, clusters, advances, offsets, direction, ligatures, reordering, combining-mark placement, fallback, embedded subsets, pagination, and rendered tolerance on all four certified platforms.
- Barcode tests decode the generated payload with an independent decoder, verify checksums and module geometry, inspect vector placement, and reject invalid input per symbology.
- Password security tests cover missing, incorrect, user and owner credentials, algorithm dictionaries, permissions, metadata handling, attachment-only modes, explicit legacy policy, and secure defaults.
- Save tests reopen every output and assert object graph and page semantics. Incremental tests assert preservation of prior revisions without requiring byte equality.
- Signed-document tests verify default read-only behavior and reject unproven incremental mutations.
- Hostile-input tests cover maximum bytes, pages, objects, depth, decompression, pixels, memory, temporary storage, time, concurrency, malformed xref data, and Worker termination.
- Scale profiles cover controlled workloads around 5,000 pages and 1 GiB with bounded temporary spill; they do not promise unbounded streaming.
- Resource tests prove module-opened resources close, caller streams remain open, Session views expire, and temporary Worker data is removed.
- Publication tests cover atomic Path replacement, stream partial-write diagnostics, multi-target COMMITTED/FAILED/NOT_ATTEMPTED receipts, callback failure, and validation failure before publication.
- Java compatibility tests compile and run the same artifacts on JDK 8, 11, 17, and 21 and reject accidental newer Java APIs.
- Public API checks compare released Native Interface and Facade signatures, enforce Automatic-Module-Name stability, and require migration notes for permitted 0.x breaks.
- Release tests build sources and Javadocs, produce signatures and checksums, generate the CycloneDX SBOM, scan licenses and vulnerabilities, and reproduce artifacts before Central upload.
- A release rehearsal creates and validates a Central bundle without auto-publishing. The first irreversible publication remains a human-approved action.
- Existing prior art is the repository's accepted ADR set, Capability terminology, Reference Suite inventory, and four-chain Acceptance Evidence design. There is no implementation test suite yet, so the first tracer bullet establishes the shared Document Workflow contract harness.

## Out of Scope

- Unchanged com.itextpdf imports.
- Binary compatibility with existing iText class files or jars.
- Byte-for-byte PDF output equality.
- Identical internal exception classes, implementation object identity, performance, or allocation behavior.
- Tracking iText 8, iText 9, or later product versions.
- Adjacent or retired products and tools including pdf2Data, pdfInvoice, pdfDebug/RUPS, DITO, and licensing infrastructure.
- Copying or adapting iText source code, resources, fixtures, or proprietary implementation details.
- Reverse engineering closed Reference Suite add-ons.
- Publishing unsupported API stubs merely to make code compile.
- PDF/A-4, PDF/UA-2, and the later standalone pdfua module.
- A public PDF/UA validator compatible with later iText versions.
- A FIPS claim in Foundation.
- Android, OSGi, and GraalVM native-image support in Foundation.
- A remote network Worker in Foundation.
- Bundling HarfBuzz, Tesseract, LibreOffice, PDFium, or other native and external engines in the default runtime.
- Guaranteeing Microsoft Office native pagination or pixel identity from the LibreOffice provider.
- OCR guarantees for handwriting or languages without an installed trained-data profile.
- Global atomicity across multiple publication destinations.
- Physical secure erasure guarantees for temporary storage.
- An unbounded-memory or unlimited-document-size promise.
- Automatic Central publication during the 0.x release process.
- Committing Central tokens, GPG passphrases, private keys, generated Maven settings, or other release credentials to the repository.

## Further Notes

- This is a program-level specification, not a single implementation ticket. Delivery follows Capability Matrix Dependency Gates rather than calendar deadlines.
- The Foundation Release version is 0.1.0 and is not a skeleton release. Every promised Foundation capability and required platform profile must be compatible before publication.
- The project knowingly retains the Folio PDF public name despite ecosystem collision risk. Discovery material uses Folio PDF by ZeroCloud and prominent non-affiliation statements.
- The canonical Maven coordinates are net.zerocloud:pdf-* and the canonical repository is https://github.com/zerocloud-sdk/folio-pdf.
- The repository was created for this specification and contains no implementation baseline yet. The local planning corpus contains the accepted domain Contexts and ADR-0001 through ADR-0032.
- The public signing key is already distributed through a Central-supported key server. The real local keyring has not yet been mutated by this specification workflow.
- The Central credential and GPG files were inspected only through metadata and redacted structural checks. No credential value appears in this issue or command output.
- Because this work spans multiple bounded contexts, native and external providers, four platform profiles, acceptance tooling, release infrastructure, and many dependency-gated milestones, the next execution route is /to-tickets rather than a single /spec-executor session.

title: [SPEC] Build Folio PDF to Reference Suite capability parity
